To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a new algorithm for scheduling periodic task systems and that this algorithm successfully schedules on any m processors any task system with utilization less than m2/(2 m - 1).

we have designed and evaluated a deadline-based scheduling policy, called the EDF-SPF policy, for scheduling periodic tasks on multiprocessors, and we have shown that the EDF- SPF policy successfully schedules any periodic task system whose utilization is at most m2 / (2m - 2).

we propose and analyze an algorithm for scheduling periodic tasks on multiprocessors, we prove that our algorithm is correct, we show that the algorithm can schedule any task system with utilization less than m2/(2 m - 1) on m processors, and we present experimental results that show that our algorithm performs well in practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the scheduling problem for periodic real-time systems on multiprocessor platforms.
the following problem: Given a set of m independent periodic tasks and a set of m processors, is it possible to schedule all the tasks such that no deadline is missed?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the problem of scheduling task systems on multipro- cessors has been solved.

the problem of scheduling a set of n independent periodic real-time tasks on m identical processors is solvable if the utilization is at most m/(m - 1) and that the problem is unsolvable if the utilization is greater than m/2.

the deadline-based algorithm presented in this thesis has a worst case ratio of at most 1.75 for any periodic task system on any number of m processors, which is optimal in the sense that no algorithm can achieve a worst case ratio less than 1.5 for any number of m.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a scheduling algorithm which has a utilization bound of 100% and a deadline bound of 200% (for the worst case).
we present a scheduling algorithm for periodic task systems on a set of m processors that is able to schedule any periodic task system that has utilization at most m 2/(2m 1).

our algorithm successfully solves the problem of scheduling any periodic task system whose utilization is less than m2/(2(m - 1)), where m is the number of processors, and the utilization of the periodic task system is defined as the sum of the utilizations of its tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deadline-based schedulers can achieve a better utilization bound than the classical EDF scheduler.
the utilization bound of m2/(2(m-1)) for multiprocessors is tight.
, for the first time, we have a deadline-based scheduling approach that can handle any utilization level on m processors.
